(a) **Freundlich Adsorption Isotherm:**
$$\frac{x}{m} = k P^{1/n} 
$$
Where $x/m$ is the mass of adsorbate adsorbed per unit mass of adsorbent, $P$ is pressure, and $k$ and $n$ are constants ($n > 1$).
* **Limitations:** It fails at high pressures where adsorption becomes independent of pressure.

(b) **Enzyme Kinetics & Michaelis-Menten Equation:**
Enzyme ($	ext{E}$) binds reversibly with Substrate ($	ext{S}$) to form a Complex ($	ext{ES}$), which then yields Product ($	ext{P}$):
$$	ext{E} + 	ext{S} \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-1}]{k_1} 	ext{ES} \xrightarrow{k_2} 	ext{E} + 	ext{P}$$

Applying steady-state approximation to $[	ext{ES}]$:
$$v = \frac{V_{\max} [S]}{K_m + [S]}$$
where $V_{\max} = k_2[	ext{E}]_0$ and $K_m = \frac{k_{-1} + k_2}{k_1}$ is the Michaelis constant.

(c) **Physisorption vs Chemisorption:**

| Feature | Physisorption | Chemisorption |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Forces** | Weak Van der Waals forces | Strong chemical bonds |
| **Enthalpy of Adsorption** | Low ($20-40 \text{ kJ/mol}$) | High ($80-400 \text{ kJ/mol}$) |
| **Reversibility** | Reversible | Irreversible |
| **Temperature Dependence** | Decreases with temperature | Increases initially with temperature |
proTip: Remember that Michaelis constant ($K_m$) represents the substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is half of its maximum ($V_{max}$).
